To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the deployment of EAP in WBAN using CS-MA/CA is not necessary and the system throughput, energy consumption, and delay performance of WBAN are better without EAP.
the performance of WBAN MAC protocol can be improved by using slotted ALOAH instead of CSMA/CA and that EAP is not necessary in most cases.

the performance of the IEEE 802. 15.6 CSMA/CA protocol under nonsaturated heterogeneous scenarios can be significantly improved by the deployment of an EAP for emergency traffic, but the overall system throughput and energy efficiency can be degraded.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and evaluation of analytical models of the performance of the IEEE 802. 15.6 standard.
the performance analysis of the MAC protocols in the WBAN environment.

the analysis of the IEEE 802. 15.6 standard for WBANs and the performance evaluation of the standard for the different user priorities and different access methods under nonsaturated heterogeneous conditions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the EAP should be used only for the highest priority class of emergency nodes, which are allowed to transmit in all the phases.
the standard is not well designed in terms of the access phase allocation for different user priorities.
EAP should be used only when there is a strict requirement for the QoS of emergency nodes, which is a rare scenario in WBAN.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the EAP is not a good option for WBANs, and it is not recommended to be used in the standard.

the performance of the IEEE 802. 15. 6 MAC protocol can be improved by the proper selection of the access phase for different user priorities, and that the performance can be further improved if the access method is changed from CSMA/CA to slotted ALOHa for the nodes having higher user priorities.
the EAP is only required in a WBAN using slotted ALOHa, and the EAP is beneficial for emergency nodes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the standard should be used in such a manner that the access phase for emergency nodes is not used by the nonemergency nodes.
the EAP should be deployed only when there is a need to provide a high level of QoS to emergency nodes.
the EAP can be used to improve the performance of WBANs with a small number of nodes and high priority traffic, such as in a hospital environment.
